title: 3. Phase 1 — Preparation
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L20: Incident Response: 3. Phase 1 — Preparation.

blocks.text: The most important phase. Everything that follows depends on what you set up before the incident.

items: IR Team — defined roles: IR Lead, analysts, forensic, legal, communications, executive sponsor
Playbooks — pre-written decision trees for common incident types (phishing, ransomware, BEC, DDoS, web compromise)
Communication plan — escalation paths, regulatory contacts, PR templates, out-of-band channels (because email may be compromised)
Forensic tools ready — DumpIt / WinPMem (memory), FTK Imager / dcfldd (disk), Wireshark (network), evidence storage
Legal contacts — internal legal counsel, external breach counsel, regulator liaisons (PDPC, NCSA in Thailand)
Tabletop exercises — practice the playbook quarterly; muscle memory matters under stress

blocks.text: Key explanation: A team that has never run a tabletop will fumble in a real incident. Practice the playbook so the mechanics are reflexive, leaving brain capacity for the unique decisions.

attribution: Course: ICCS423 | Source: Thoth + RAG | Target: 3rd-4th year CS | Date: 2026-05-03
